frictions.title: When2meet schedule grid cells lack accessible names, roles, and focusability
frictions.description: The availability schedule grid presents time slots as unlabelled plain HTML div elements without ARIA grid semantics, accessible names, keyboard focusability, or state announcements, preventing VoiceOver users from discovering or toggling availability slots.

interventions.description: Make schedule grid cells keyboard-accessible with ARIA grid roles, date/time labels, and toggle actions for screen readers.

The availability schedule grid represents slots as plain div elements with no ARIA grid role, accessible name, tabindex, or programmatic state. A VoiceOver user using linear navigation repeatedly pressed VO+Space and Enter to toggle availability, but the application gave no focus, no spoken description, and no selection change. As a result, the scheduling grid is effectively unusable nonvisually, forcing the user to abandon the interface.
interventions.mitigation: Give the schedule grid proper ARIA semantics so each time slot is exposed as an interactive control: assign role="grid" to the slot container, role="row" to each row, and role="gridcell" with tabindex="0" to each slot element. Compute an accessible name for each cell (for example, combining the date header, time row, and current availability state such as 'Friday, Aug 14, 9:00 AM: Available'). Bind keyboard handling for Enter and Space to toggle the slot and update its state (e.g., aria-pressed or a corresponding label change) so that screen reader announcements reflect the new value. Ensure the interaction also works with mouse events by reusing the same toggle logic.

frictions.title: Sign-in form inputs lack accessible labels in VoiceOver Rotor
frictions.description: The 'Your Name' and 'Password' text input fields on the When2meet page lack programmatic label associations (<label> or aria-label), causing them to be omitted from the Form Controls list when navigating via the VoiceOver Rotor menu (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Add accessible labels to the sign-in form input fields.

The 'Your Name' and 'Password' text input fields on the When2meet sign-in form lack programmatic label associations, so they do not appear when the user opens the VoiceOver Rotor and selects the Form Controls menu. This omission occurred repeatedly during sequential navigation sessions. The consequence is that a VoiceOver user cannot discover or directly target these fields through standard form-control navigation, and must instead tab through the page or use other indirect navigation methods to reach the sign-in inputs.
interventions.mitigation: Associate each sign-in input with a programmatically determinable accessible name, for example by wrapping the field in a <label> element or adding an aria-label attribute. Ensure the accessible name is announced and that both fields appear in the VoiceOver Form Controls rotor menu. If the password field is meant to be optional, its label should clearly say so, but the association must still exist.

frictions.title: When2meet page lacks ARIA landmarks for VoiceOver Rotor navigation
frictions.description: The When2meet page contains no ARIA landmarks or HTML5 sectioning elements, causing VoiceOver's Landmarks rotor menu to announce 'No items in, Landmarks menu' when queried and preventing structural section navigation (WCAG 1.3.1, 2.4.1).

interventions.description: Add ARIA landmark roles to major sections of the When2meet page.

The When2meet web page does not expose any ARIA landmarks or HTML5 sectioning elements. When the user opens the VoiceOver Rotor and selects the Landmarks menu, VoiceOver announces 'No items in, Landmarks menu', and the user cannot jump directly to major page sections (header, main content, grids). The consequence is that the user must sequentially traverse the whole page or rely on other rotor categories, making navigation slower and more disorienting.
interventions.mitigation: Add appropriate ARIA landmark roles to the major layout containers: a banner landmark for the page header, a navigation landmark for the menu, a main landmark for the core content, and labeled region landmarks for the user availability grid and shared availability grid. Verify with VoiceOver that these sections appear in the Landmarks rotor menu and can be reached directly.

blind.description: The Elfsight photo-gallery carousel exposes each slide as a generic `div role="button" aria-label="Visit linked content"` (repeated many times because Swiper duplicates slides), so a screen-reader user hears a dozen identical, purpose-less controls with no idea of the destination.

The Elfsight previous/next controls are `div role="button" aria-label="Previous"/"Next"` with no `tabindex`, so they are not focusable and a keyboard/screen-reader user cannot move through that gallery at all.

Both the desktop and mobile header markup (plus the overlay menu) are present in the DOM, so the Shop/Books/Playground/About links, the "Login" link and the "0 items in cart" link are announced two to three times, and the two `background-pause-button` pairs expose both "Pause Background" and "Play Background" simultaneously, creating duplicated, contradictory controls.
The menu toggle button computes the name "Open Menu Close Menu" (both spans read) and carries no `aria-expanded`, so its purpose and open/closed state are not conveyed.

Decorative scrolling marquee phrases are marked up as multiple `<h1>` elements ("Motor Skill Development", "•", "Multi-Lingual Content") and "Why Little Leaders?" is another h1, so heading navigation returns meaningless, duplicated headings instead of a real page structure.

low_vision.description: The marquee block scrolls its heading text continuously along an SVG path with no pause/stop control, making the text impossible to read at magnification.

Two auto-rotating carousels (the Elfsight swiper gallery and the `user-items-list-carousel` with its "Item 1 of 8" live region) change content on their own, so magnified users lose the item they were reading.

Long white bold testimonial text (`sqsrte-text-color--white`) sits directly over a photographic section background (`image-asset.jpg`) with only a translucent overlay, so contrast varies and can fall below 4.5:1.

Headings use Squarespace viewport-scaled text (`sqsrte-scaled-text-container`) and fluid image blocks, so text size is tied to container width rather than user text settings and can clip or fail to enlarge when zoomed/resized.

The transparent sticky header (`tweak-transparent-header`, `tweak-fixed-header-style-scroll-back`) overlays page content and consumes a large share of the viewport at high zoom, obscuring content beneath it.

dhh.description: The embedded Vimeo videos ("Little Leaders Classics Video Series (Official Trailer)" and "Why Little Leaders?") are presented with no indication of captions, so their narration, music and dialogue are inaccessible.

No transcript or text alternative accompanies either video block — the only adjacent text is the credit "A message from our founder, Bradley Silvius" — so the spoken content of the founder's message is unavailable.

motor.description: The Elfsight gallery relies on Swiper drag/swipe plus `div role="button"` arrows that are not in the tab order, leaving no keyboard or single-pointer alternative for browsing its slides.
The marquee's clickable hitbox path and the auto-advancing carousels move continuously, forcing users to hit a moving target with no way to stop the motion first.

Interactive icons are small and thin — the cart icon, the hairline SVG carousel arrows (`user-items-list-carousel__arrow-icon`, 24×14 mobile arrows) and the Elfsight 16×16 arrow icons — making accurate pointer activation difficult.
Footer links are packed inline with only whitespace between them (`Privacy Policy Terms and Conditions`), so adjacent targets are effectively touching and easy to mis-click.

Because both desktop and mobile header blocks plus the overlay menu are all in the DOM, keyboard users must tab through triplicated nav links, "Login" (an inert `href="#"` link) and cart links before reaching content, greatly increasing keystrokes and dead-end activations.

VoiceOver announces 'Visit linked content button' repeatedly during both rotor and sequential Tab navigation, making targets indistinguishable (WCAG 2.4.6, 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Remove generic aria-label from gallery buttons so VoiceOver announces their specific nested image alt text.

On the Little Leaders homepage (www.littleleaders.com), each item container in the photo gallery carousel widget sets aria-label="Visit linked content". This generic accessible name overrides the specific alt text of the image content nested inside each item, so VoiceOver announces 'Visit linked content, button' repeatedly for every carousel control during both rotor (Form Controls) exploration and sequential Tab/Shift+Tab navigation. The user could not distinguish one gallery target from another and had to fall back to trial-and-error tabbing to find the link to the Shop page, increasing navigation effort and the chance of activating unintended content.
interventions.mitigation: Remove the hard-coded aria-label="Visit linked content" from the gallery item containers (observed as the photo-gallery item component elements in the Elfsight widget) so each control inherits its accessible name from the descriptive alt text of the image it wraps; alternatively, programmatically set each container's accessible name to that specific image alt text (e.g., 'Little Leaders Characters', 'Little Leaders Videos'). Each carousel control would then be announced with a unique, meaningful label in the VoiceOver rotor and in sequential keyboard navigation.

interventions.description: The Click Captcha challenge is provided only as an image with no accessible text alternative or nonvisual way to identify the objects to click. VoiceOver announced the image as 'content is empty', so the screen reader user could not determine which areas of the image represent valid targets. Repeatedly activating the Check button with VO+Space produced no progress because the challenge logic cannot be completed without visual identification of image content. This blocks assistive technology users from passing the CAPTCHA and submitting the form.
interventions.mitigation: Provide a nonvisual alternative mechanism for the CAPTCHA challenge, such as an audio-based or text-based challenge that does not rely on seeing the image. If the image is part of the required task, give it an appropriate text alternative or accessible description conveying the challenge instruction. Also expose each selectable object as a semantically named, keyboard-focusable element (for example, buttons or links with descriptive labels) so the entire challenge can be operated with a keyboard, and ensure the result of pressing Check is announced through a status region or live region.

blind.description: The banner contains an empty top-level heading (`<span role="heading" aria-level="1">` with no text) while the real page heading "Flight search" (class HeMQ4) is visually hidden, so heading-based navigation lands on a blank "heading level 1" and gives no orientation.

The date picker exposes day cells as `role="gridcell"` wrapping inner `role="button" tabindex="-1"` elements, with weekday header row and many cells marked `aria-hidden="true"` and no grid accessible name, so screen-reader users cannot reliably read or choose a departure/return date.

The "Loading results" progressbars (`role="progressbar" aria-label="Loading results" aria-hidden="true"`) are hidden from AT, so the asynchronous fetching and arrival of the 23 flight results is not announced.

The ticket-type and cabin-class widgets are custom comboboxes whose `aria-controls` points at an empty `aria-hidden="true"` listbox (ids i9 / i22) while the real options live in a separate `ul`, and the combobox itself carries `aria-live="polite"`, producing wrong or duplicated announcements of the available/selected values.

Primary navigation is built from `<button ... role="link">` items (Explore, Flights, Hotels) and duplicated in the drawer as `div role="link" tabindex="0"` with labels like "Selected Tab: Flights", giving conflicting role/state semantics and a second, redundant navigation set to screen-reader users.

low_vision.description: The viewport meta sets `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, preventing pinch/browser zoom of the flight search UI on touch devices.
The date-picker dialog renders several full month grids (July–October…) side by side in a fixed-width scrolling panel, forcing both horizontal and vertical scrolling once magnified.

Icon-only controls (swap origin/destination, add multiple airports, change appearance, calendar month chevrons) convey their purpose only through hover-triggered tooltips (`EY8ABd-OWXEXe-TAWMXe`, `aria-hidden="true"` until hover) that a magnifier user may never see or that disappear on pointer movement.

Calendar state such as the chosen departure day is signalled only by background/color styling classes (e.g. `Ic3tg NXzzqb g7lVZ` on August 18), with no visible non-color indicator, making the selection hard to spot when zoomed or in low contrast.

Key controls use very small glyphs and dense text (16–18px SVG stepper and remove icons, single-letter weekday headers, tiny "Aged 2-11" secondary labels), which pixelate/clip badly under screen magnification.

motor.description: Selecting travel dates requires hitting tiny, tightly packed day cells in the month grids (`div.WhDFk` gridcells), whose inner activatable `role="button"` is `tabindex="-1"`, so imprecise pointer users have no reliably large target or simple tab-stop alternative.

The calendar's month/step chevron buttons are `tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"` inside containers wired to `mousedown`/hover handlers, so they are effectively pointer-hover-only with no keyboard-operable equivalent.

Passenger counts must be set by repeatedly clicking 16px `+`/`−` icon buttons ("Add adult", "Remove infant on lap") that sit immediately next to each other, demanding repeated precise clicks with no direct numeric entry.

Origin/destination chips place a small `role="button"` "Remove" control (16px X icon) inside the selected `role="option"` item, so a slightly off-target click deletes the chosen city instead of selecting it.

Several essential controls are non-native `div role="button"/role="link" tabindex="0"` (Main menu, Google apps, drawer items), relying entirely on scripted key handling, so keyboard-only or switch users may be unable to activate them with Enter/Space.
